To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have developed and validated a new, efficient and accurate, parameter-free method for the segmentation of cellular structures in 3D electron tomograms.
we have developed a parameter-free, fast, 3D edge detection filter, which is suitable for the automated segmentation and annotation of macromolecular structures from cellular electron tomograms.

the 3D implementation (1) of the parameter-free bilateral edge detection algorithm is a robust and efficient method for the rapid and reliable segmentation of complex cellular tomograms, (2) is capable of detecting edges as small as 2 pixels, (3) is capable of identifying edges with signal intensity as low as 2.4% above the mean background signal, and (4) can be used to identify macromolecular assemblies within cellular tomograms at high resolution.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the application of image processing and analysis techniques to biological data sets, in particular electron tomograms.

the development of new image analysis techniques for the automated analysis of cellular tomograms and the accurate identification of cellular structures and macromolecular assemblies at high resolution in 3D.
the development of new methods for the automated segmentation and analysis of 3D cellular ultrastructural data sets.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the 3D bilateral edge detection filter is a powerful and robust tool that can be applied to any cellular tomogram for automated segmentation of cellular structures.
the 3D bilateral filter is the best filter available for the segmentation of cellular tomogram data.
the 3D bilateral edge detection filter provides a robust and accurate method for the automated and parameter-free segmentation of cellular tomographic data.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the 3D bilateral edge detection (BLE) filter is the first parameter-free 3D filter that can be applied to cellular tomograms to accurately identify macromolecular structures at the nanoscale.
the 3D implementation is an efficient and reliable filter for the segmentation of macromolecular structures in cellular tomograms.
we have developed a new 3D image filter that is able to detect edges in cellular tomograms with high sensitivity and accuracy and without the need of any parameter input.
The main takeaway from our work is that

3D image processing is a key step for the analysis of cellular tomograms, and that the 3D image filter we present in this paper is a valuable addition to the current repertoire of 3D image segmentation methods.
the 3D bilateral edge-detection filter is a robust tool for the automated segmentation and annotation of cellular tomograms.

a parameter-free, high-throughput method for the accurate identification of macromolecular structures from cellular tomograms can be achieved by applying the 3D bilateral edge-detection filter to the tomographic data set.
